families.label: Document
families.summary: The three tags every page is built on.

families.label: Metadata
families.summary: Invisible setup in the head that tells the browser how to treat the page.

families.label: Sectioning
families.summary: Landmarks and headings that give a page its outline.

families.label: Grouping
families.summary: Block-level containers for paragraphs, lists and figures.

families.label: Tables
families.summary: Rows and columns for tabular data.

families.label: Embedded
families.summary: Media and external content pulled into the page.

families.label: Text-level
families.summary: Inline tags that add meaning to words inside a sentence.

families.label: Edits
families.summary: Marks text that was added to or removed from a document.

families.label: Forms
families.summary: Controls that collect input. Many states, many attributes.

families.label: Interactive
families.summary: Built-in widgets that react to the user without JavaScript.

families.label: Scripting
families.summary: Tags that bring in code or change the elements around them.

families.label: Obsolete
families.summary: Removed from the standard. Parked below the table like lanthanides and actinides.

elements.name: HTML root
elements.summary: The root of every HTML document. Every other element sits inside it.
elements.tip: Always set the lang attribute. Screen readers use it to pick a voice and pronunciation.

elements.name: Head
elements.summary: Holds metadata the browser reads but does not display, such as the title, styles and scripts.
elements.tip: Put the charset meta tag first. The browser must know the encoding before it reads anything else.

elements.name: Body
elements.summary: Holds everything the user sees and interacts with.
elements.tip: A page has exactly one body. Styling it is fine, but layout usually belongs on main or a wrapper.

elements.name: Title
elements.summary: Sets the text shown in the browser tab, bookmarks and search results.
elements.tip: Put the specific part first, such as "Pricing | Acme". Tabs truncate from the right.

elements.name: Base URL
elements.summary: Sets the starting URL that every relative link on the page resolves against.
elements.tip: Rarely worth it. It silently changes every relative link, including #anchor links.

elements.name: Link
elements.summary: Connects the page to an outside resource. Stylesheets, icons, fonts and preloads all use it.
elements.tip: The rel attribute decides what it does. rel="preload" fetches early, rel="stylesheet" applies styles.

elements.name: Metadata
elements.summary: Carries facts about the page, such as its encoding, viewport, description and social previews.
elements.tip: Without the viewport meta tag, phones render the page at desktop width and shrink it.

elements.name: Style
elements.summary: Holds CSS written directly in the page.
elements.tip: Good for small critical styles. Larger stylesheets cache better as separate files.

elements.name: Main content
elements.summary: Wraps the main content of the page, the part unique to this URL.
elements.tip: Use one visible main per page. Screen reader users jump straight to it.

elements.name: Header
elements.summary: Introductory content for the page or a section, usually a logo, title or navigation.
elements.tip: It only becomes the banner landmark when it is not inside article, aside, main, nav or section.

elements.name: Footer
elements.summary: Closing content for the page or a section, such as copyright, links or author info.
elements.tip: Like header, it is only a landmark at the page level.

elements.name: Navigation
elements.summary: Marks a block of major navigation links.
elements.tip: Not every group of links needs it. Save it for menus, breadcrumbs and tables of contents.

elements.name: Article
elements.summary: A self-contained piece that would make sense on its own, like a post, comment or product card.
elements.tip: Test it this way. If you could syndicate it in an RSS feed, it is an article.

elements.name: Section
elements.summary: A themed chunk of a document, normally with its own heading.
elements.tip: If it has no heading, you probably wanted a div.

elements.name: Aside
elements.summary: Content related to the surrounding content but not part of its main flow, like a sidebar or pull quote.
elements.tip: Being on the side visually does not make something an aside. The relationship matters, not the position.

elements.name: Search
elements.summary: Wraps a search or filter form and marks it as the search landmark.
elements.tip: Added in 2023. It replaces the old pattern of role="search" on a form or div.

elements.name: Heading 1
elements.summary: The top-level heading. Names what the whole page is about.
elements.tip: Use one per page. Pick heading levels for structure, then style them with CSS.

elements.name: Heading 2
elements.summary: A major section heading under the h1.
elements.tip: Screen reader users skim a page by jumping between headings, so the order should read like a table of contents.

elements.name: Heading 3
elements.summary: A subsection heading under an h2.
elements.tip: Do not skip levels to get a smaller font. Going from h2 to h4 breaks the outline.

elements.name: Heading 4
elements.summary: A heading under an h3.
elements.tip: If you are this deep often, the page may be doing too much.

elements.name: Heading 5
elements.summary: A heading under an h4.
elements.tip: Rare in practice. Mostly seen in long technical documents.

elements.name: Heading 6
elements.summary: The lowest heading level.
elements.tip: There is no h7. Past this level, use the heading role with aria-level.

elements.name: Heading group
elements.summary: Groups a heading with a subtitle or tagline written in p elements.
elements.tip: Only one heading goes inside. The subtitle is a paragraph, not a second heading.

elements.name: Contact address
elements.summary: Contact information for the nearest article or the whole page.
elements.tip: It is for contact details only. A random postal address in a sentence does not belong here.

elements.name: Paragraph
elements.summary: A paragraph of text.
elements.tip: A p cannot contain block elements. The browser closes it early if you nest a div inside.

elements.name: Thematic break
elements.summary: A shift in topic between paragraphs, like a scene change in a story.
elements.tip: Use a CSS border for purely decorative lines. Screen readers announce hr as a separator.

elements.name: Preformatted text
elements.summary: Displays text exactly as written, keeping every space and line break.
elements.tip: Wrap code blocks as pre containing code. Long lines need overflow-x: auto or they break the layout.

elements.name: Block quotation
elements.summary: A long quotation from another source.
elements.tip: Browsers do not display the cite attribute. Put a visible attribution in a figcaption or footer.

elements.name: Ordered list
elements.summary: A list where the order matters, like steps in a recipe.
elements.tip: Use start and reversed instead of typing numbers by hand.

elements.name: Unordered list
elements.summary: A list where the order does not matter.
elements.tip: Safari drops list semantics when you set list-style: none. Add role="list" if the count matters to users.

elements.name: Menu
elements.summary: A list of commands or toolbar buttons. Browsers treat it exactly like ul.
elements.tip: It was deprecated, then revived. It does not create a dropdown menu on its own.

elements.name: List item
elements.summary: One item in an ol, ul or menu.
elements.tip: Its only valid parents are ol, ul and menu.

elements.name: Description list
elements.summary: A list of name and value pairs, such as a glossary or a spec sheet.
elements.tip: You may wrap each dt and dd pair in a div for styling. That is valid.

elements.name: Description term
elements.summary: The name half of a pair in a dl.
elements.tip: Several dt elements can share one dd, for synonyms.

elements.name: Description details
elements.summary: The value half of a pair in a dl.
elements.tip: One dt can have several dd elements, for multiple meanings.

elements.name: Figure
elements.summary: Self-contained content referenced from the main text, such as an image, chart or code sample.
elements.tip: Not every image is a figure. Use it when the content could move to an appendix without breaking the text.

elements.name: Figure caption
elements.summary: The caption for a figure.
elements.tip: It must be the first or last child of the figure. It does not replace an image's alt text.

elements.name: Division
elements.summary: A generic block container with no meaning. It exists for styling and scripting hooks.
elements.tip: The most used element on the web. Reach for it last, after checking whether a semantic element fits.

elements.name: Table
elements.summary: Data arranged in rows and columns.
elements.tip: For data only. Tables for page layout died with the 2000s.

elements.name: Table caption
elements.summary: The title of a table.
elements.tip: It must be the first child of table. It gives the table its accessible name.

elements.name: Column group
elements.summary: Groups columns so you can style them together.
elements.tip: Only a few CSS properties work on columns, mainly background, border, width and visibility.

elements.name: Column
elements.summary: One column, or several with span, inside a colgroup.
elements.tip: Handy for setting column widths in one place.

elements.name: Table head
elements.summary: The header rows of a table.
elements.tip: With position: sticky on its cells, headers stay visible while the user scrolls.

elements.name: Table body
elements.summary: The main body rows of a table.
elements.tip: The browser adds one if you leave it out, which can surprise CSS selectors like table > tr.

elements.name: Table foot
elements.summary: Summary rows at the bottom of a table, like totals.
elements.tip: When printed, browsers can repeat thead and tfoot on every page.

elements.name: Table row
elements.summary: One row of cells.
elements.tip: Rows hold td and th cells only.

elements.name: Table data cell
elements.summary: One cell of data.
elements.tip: For complex tables, link cells to their headers with the headers attribute.

elements.name: Table header cell
elements.summary: A header cell that labels a row or column.
elements.tip: Set scope="col" or scope="row" so screen readers announce the right header with each cell.

elements.name: Picture
elements.summary: Wraps several image sources so the browser can pick the best one for the screen or format support.
elements.tip: It needs an img inside. The img provides the alt text and the fallback.

elements.name: Media source
elements.summary: One candidate file for a picture, video or audio element.
elements.tip: The browser takes the first source that matches. Order them from most to least preferred.

elements.name: Image
elements.summary: Embeds an image.
elements.tip: Always include alt. Use alt="" for decorative images. Set width and height to stop the layout jumping.

elements.name: Inline frame
elements.summary: Embeds another web page inside the current one, like a map or video player.
elements.tip: Give it a title for screen readers. Add sandbox when you do not trust the content.

elements.name: Embed
elements.summary: Embeds external content handled by a plugin or the browser, such as a PDF.
elements.tip: A leftover from the plugin era. Prefer img, video, audio or iframe.

elements.name: Object
elements.summary: Embeds an external resource with fallback content inside it.
elements.tip: Still useful for showing a PDF with a download link as the fallback.

elements.name: Video
elements.summary: Plays video with built-in controls.
elements.tip: Browsers block autoplay with sound. Add muted if you need autoplay, and captions with track.

elements.name: Audio
elements.summary: Plays sound with built-in controls.
elements.tip: Without the controls attribute it is invisible. Provide a transcript for spoken content.

elements.name: Text track
elements.summary: Adds captions, subtitles or chapters to a video or audio element, from a WebVTT file.
elements.tip: Captions are the single biggest accessibility win for video.

elements.name: Image map
elements.summary: Defines clickable regions on an image, together with area.
elements.tip: Regions do not scale with responsive images. An SVG with links usually works better.

elements.name: Image map area
elements.summary: One clickable region inside a map.
elements.tip: Each area needs alt text, just like an image.

elements.name: Scalable Vector Graphics
elements.summary: Inline vector graphics. Icons, charts and illustrations that stay sharp at any size.
elements.tip: It brings its own language of elements. Add role="img" and a title, or aria-hidden="true" if decorative.

elements.name: MathML
elements.summary: Inline mathematical notation that screen readers can read aloud.
elements.tip: All major browsers support MathML Core now. It beats equations baked into images.

elements.name: Anchor
elements.summary: A hyperlink to another page, a file, an email address or a spot on the same page.
elements.tip: Without href it is not a link and is not focusable. If it does something rather than goes somewhere, use a button.

elements.name: Emphasis
elements.summary: Stress emphasis that changes the meaning of a sentence, the way you would stress a word out loud.
elements.tip: If you only want italics, use i or CSS.

elements.name: Strong importance
elements.summary: Marks text as important, serious or urgent.
elements.tip: Use it for warnings and key facts. Bold for style alone belongs to b or CSS.

elements.name: Side comment
elements.summary: Fine print, such as legal text, disclaimers and copyright lines.
elements.tip: It means side comment, not smaller font. Do not use it for headings or subtitles.

elements.name: Strikethrough
elements.summary: Text that is no longer accurate, like an old price next to a sale price.
elements.tip: For tracked edits to a document, use del instead.

elements.name: Citation
elements.summary: The title of a creative work, such as a book, film, song or paper.
elements.tip: It is for the work's title, not the person who wrote it.

elements.name: Inline quotation
elements.summary: A short quotation inside a sentence. Browsers add the quote marks for you.
elements.tip: Do not type quote marks around it or you get doubles.

elements.name: Definition
elements.summary: The spot where a term is defined in the text.
elements.tip: Use it once per term, at the definition. Later mentions are plain text or a link back.

elements.name: Abbreviation
elements.summary: An abbreviation or acronym, with the full form in the title attribute.
elements.tip: Touch and keyboard users never see title tooltips. Spell it out in the text on first use.

elements.name: Ruby annotation
elements.summary: Small pronunciation notes above or beside characters, common in Japanese and Chinese text.
elements.tip: Pair it with rt for the note and rp for fallback parentheses.

elements.name: Ruby text
elements.summary: The annotation text inside a ruby element.
elements.tip: Only valid inside ruby.

elements.name: Ruby parenthesis
elements.summary: Fallback parentheses shown only by browsers that cannot render ruby.
elements.tip: Every modern browser supports ruby, so these mostly stay hidden.

elements.name: Data
elements.summary: Attaches a machine-readable value to human-readable text, like a product ID behind a product name.
elements.tip: For dates and times, use time instead.

elements.name: Time
elements.summary: A date, time or duration, with a machine-readable version in datetime.
elements.tip: Search engines and calendar tools read the datetime attribute. Use ISO format, like 2026-10-02.

elements.name: Code
elements.summary: A fragment of computer code.
elements.tip: For multi-line code, put it inside pre. Code alone collapses whitespace.

elements.name: Variable
elements.summary: A variable in math or code, like the x in an equation.
elements.tip: Rarely used, but it is the right tag for placeholders in docs.

elements.name: Sample output
elements.summary: Output from a program, such as an error message.
elements.tip: Pairs well with kbd when documenting terminal sessions.

elements.name: Keyboard input
elements.summary: Keys or text the user should type, like Ctrl + C.
elements.tip: Nest kbd elements for key combos. Each key gets its own kbd.

elements.name: Subscript
elements.summary: Lowered text, as in H₂O.
elements.tip: Use it when the position carries meaning. For styling only, use CSS.

elements.name: Superscript
elements.summary: Raised text, as in exponents and footnote markers.
elements.tip: Footnote links inside sup need a clear label for screen readers.

elements.name: Idiomatic text
elements.summary: Text in a different voice, like foreign words, ship names or thoughts.
elements.tip: Icon fonts hijacked it for years. It is fine for icons only when they have aria-hidden="true".

elements.name: Bring attention
elements.summary: Draws attention to text without adding importance, like keywords in a summary.
elements.tip: If the text matters more, use strong.

elements.name: Unarticulated annotation
elements.summary: Text with a non-textual annotation, like a misspelled word flagged with a squiggle.
elements.tip: Underlined text looks like a link. Avoid it unless the meaning calls for it.

elements.name: Mark
elements.summary: Highlights text relevant to the current context, like search matches.
elements.tip: Most screen readers do not announce it. Add hidden text if the highlight matters.

elements.name: Bidirectional isolate
elements.summary: Isolates text whose direction is unknown, such as a user name that might be Arabic or Hebrew.
elements.tip: Use it around any user-generated name shown inside a sentence.

elements.name: Bidirectional override
elements.summary: Forces text to render in the direction set by its dir attribute.
elements.tip: The dir attribute is required. Without it, bdo does nothing.

elements.name: Span
elements.summary: A generic inline container with no meaning.
elements.tip: The inline twin of div. Check the text-level tags above before using it.

elements.name: Line break
elements.summary: A line break where it is part of the content, as in poems and postal addresses.
elements.tip: Do not use it for spacing. Use margins.

elements.name: Word break opportunity
elements.summary: A spot where the browser may break a long word or URL if it needs to.
elements.tip: Handy inside long URLs and file paths that would otherwise overflow.

elements.name: Inserted text
elements.summary: Text added to a document after it was first published.
elements.tip: Screen readers often skip it silently. Add visually hidden text like "added" if the change matters.

elements.name: Deleted text
elements.summary: Text removed from a document, kept visible to show the change.
elements.tip: For outdated info that was never an edit, like an old price, use s.

elements.name: Form
elements.summary: Groups inputs and sends their values to a server.
elements.tip: A real form gives you Enter-to-submit, validation and autofill for free. Do not fake one with divs.

elements.name: Label
elements.summary: The visible name of a form control.
elements.tip: Clicking a label focuses its input. Placeholder text is not a label.

elements.name: Input
elements.summary: A single form control. Its type turns it into a text box, checkbox, date picker, slider and twenty more.
elements.tip: The heaviest element on the table. Pick the right type, like email or tel, to get the right phone keyboard.

elements.name: Button
elements.summary: A clickable control that does something, like submit a form or open a dialog.
elements.tip: Inside a form, the default type is submit. Set type="button" for anything else.

elements.name: Select
elements.summary: A dropdown or list of options to choose from.
elements.tip: Newer browsers let you fully style it with appearance: base-select.

elements.name: Data list
elements.summary: Suggested values for an input, shown as autocomplete hints.
elements.tip: Users can still type anything. It suggests, it does not restrict.

elements.name: Option group
elements.summary: Groups related options inside a select under a heading.
elements.tip: The label shows as a heading and cannot be selected.

elements.name: Option
elements.summary: One choice in a select or datalist.
elements.tip: Without value, the option's text is what gets submitted.

elements.name: Text area
elements.summary: A multi-line text box.
elements.tip: field-sizing: content lets it grow with the text, no JavaScript needed.

elements.name: Output
elements.summary: The result of a calculation or user action, like a total price.
elements.tip: Screen readers announce changes to it automatically, because it is a live region.

elements.name: Progress bar
elements.summary: Shows how far a task has come, like an upload.
elements.tip: Leave out value for an indeterminate spinner-style bar.

elements.name: Meter
elements.summary: A measurement within a known range, like disk usage or password strength.
elements.tip: Not for progress. Use progress when something is moving toward done.

elements.name: Field set
elements.summary: Groups related controls, like a set of radio buttons.
elements.tip: Disabling the fieldset disables every control inside it.

elements.name: Legend
elements.summary: The caption for a fieldset.
elements.tip: Screen readers read it before each control in the group, so keep it short.

elements.name: Selected content
elements.summary: Mirrors the chosen option's content inside a customizable select's button.
elements.tip: New in 2025. Lets a styled select show icons or rich content for the current choice.

elements.name: Details
elements.summary: A disclosure widget that shows or hides content when clicked.
elements.tip: Give several details the same name and they act as an accordion. Only one stays open.

elements.name: Summary
elements.summary: The always-visible label of a details element. Clicking it toggles the content.
elements.tip: It must be the first child of details. Do not put buttons or links inside it.

elements.name: Dialog
elements.summary: A modal or non-modal dialog box.
elements.tip: Open it with showModal() to get focus trapping, a backdrop and Escape-to-close for free.

elements.name: Script
elements.summary: Runs JavaScript, either inline or from a file.
elements.tip: A plain script in the head blocks rendering. Use defer or type="module".

elements.name: No script
elements.summary: Content shown only when JavaScript is turned off.
elements.tip: It does not help when JavaScript fails to load. It only checks whether scripting is enabled.

elements.name: Template
elements.summary: Inert HTML that the browser parses but does not render, ready for JavaScript to clone.
elements.tip: With shadowrootmode it builds a shadow root right in the HTML, no JavaScript needed.

elements.name: Slot
elements.summary: A placeholder inside a web component where outside content appears.
elements.tip: Only works inside a shadow root.

elements.name: Canvas
elements.summary: A drawing surface for graphics made with JavaScript, like games and charts.
elements.tip: Screen readers see nothing inside. Put fallback content or a text alternative between the tags.

elements.name: Acronym
elements.summary: Marked an acronym, like NASA.
elements.tip: Merged into abbr because nobody agreed on what separated an acronym from an abbreviation.

elements.name: Java applet
elements.summary: Embedded a Java program in the page.
elements.tip: Browsers dropped Java plugins around 2015.

elements.name: Base font
elements.summary: Set the default font for the whole page.
elements.tip: CSS inheritance made it pointless.

elements.name: Background sound
elements.summary: Played background music when the page loaded. Internet Explorer only.
elements.tip: The reason people muted their speakers in 1998.

elements.name: Big text
elements.summary: Made text one size larger.
elements.tip: Pure presentation. Its sibling small survived because it was redefined as fine print.

elements.name: Blink
elements.summary: Made text flash on and off. Netscape only.
elements.tip: Flashing content can trigger seizures. WCAG forbids it.

elements.name: Center
elements.summary: Centered its contents.
elements.tip: Still on about 4.5% of pages in 2024, according to the Web Almanac.

elements.name: Directory list
elements.summary: A list of file names in a directory.
elements.tip: Browsers always rendered it as a ul anyway.

elements.name: Font
elements.summary: Set the color, typeface and size of text.
elements.tip: Tied with center as the most used obsolete element, on about 4.5% of pages in 2024.

elements.name: Frame
elements.summary: One pane inside a frameset.
elements.tip: Frames broke bookmarks, the back button and search engines.

elements.name: Frame set
elements.summary: Split the window into frames, each loading a separate page.
elements.tip: It replaced body entirely. A page had one or the other.

elements.name: Image alias
elements.summary: A misspelling of img that browsers learned to accept.
elements.tip: Parsers still quietly rewrite it to img.

elements.name: Index search
elements.summary: A one-field search box that predated forms.
elements.tip: One of the oldest tags on the web.

elements.name: Key generator
elements.summary: Generated a key pair for client certificates when a form was submitted.
elements.tip: Added in HTML5, removed a few years later. A short life.

elements.name: Listing
elements.summary: Displayed source code listings.
elements.tip: pre did the same job and won.

elements.name: Marquee
elements.summary: Scrolled text across the screen. Internet Explorer's answer to blink.
elements.tip: Browsers still render it. That does not mean you should.

elements.name: Menu item
elements.summary: A command in a context menu.
elements.tip: Only Firefox ever shipped it, and then removed it.

elements.name: Multiple columns
elements.summary: Flowed text into newspaper-style columns. Netscape only.
elements.tip: CSS multi-column layout does this properly.

elements.name: Next ID
elements.summary: Helped early HTML editors generate unique anchor names.
elements.tip: A fossil from Tim Berners-Lee's NeXT editor.

elements.name: No break
elements.summary: Stopped text from wrapping to a new line.
elements.tip: Still on about 0.8% of pages in 2024.

elements.name: No embed
elements.summary: Fallback for browsers that could not handle embed.
elements.tip: object holds its own fallback, which made this redundant.

elements.name: No frames
elements.summary: Fallback for browsers that could not show frames.
elements.tip: Died with frameset.

elements.name: Parameter
elements.summary: Passed settings to plugins inside object or applet.
elements.tip: Removed in 2023 once plugins were gone.

elements.name: Plain text
elements.summary: Treated everything after it as plain text, for the rest of the file.
elements.tip: It has no closing tag. Nothing can end it.

elements.name: Ruby base
elements.summary: Marked the base text in a ruby annotation.
elements.tip: Unnecessary, because ruby treats its plain text as the base.

elements.name: Ruby text container
elements.summary: Grouped several rt annotations together.
elements.tip: Browser support never arrived.

elements.name: Spacer
elements.summary: Inserted blank space. Netscape only.
elements.tip: Its cousin, the transparent spacer.gif, lived much longer.

elements.name: Strike
elements.summary: Drew a line through text.
elements.tip: The short form s survived. This one did not.

elements.name: Teletype
elements.summary: Rendered text in a monospace font.
elements.tip: Replaced by tags that say why the text is monospace.

elements.name: Example
elements.summary: Showed HTML source without needing to escape the angle brackets.
elements.tip: Browsers still honor it. Some developers miss it.
